questions.question: The process by which the eye lens changes its focal length to focus on near or distant objects is called __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Accommodation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The ability of the **eye lens** to adjust its **focal length** to focus on both near and distant objects is called **Accommodation**.
 
• This process is facilitated by the **ciliary muscles**, which can modify the curvature of the **crystalline lens**.
 
• When the **ciliary muscles** are relaxed, the lens becomes **thin** and its **focal length increases**, allowing the eye to see **distant objects** clearly.
 
• When the **ciliary muscles contract**, the lens becomes **thicker** and its **focal length decreases**, enabling the eye to focus on **nearby objects**.
 
• The **power of accommodation** for a normal human eye is limited; for a healthy adult, the closest distance an object can be seen clearly without strain is about **25 cm**.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Accommodation__.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Near Point and Far Point**:
 
 
• The **near point** of the eye (least distance of distinct vision) is **25 cm** for a normal young adult.
 
• The **far point** of a normal eye is **infinity**, meaning it can see objects at a very great distance clearly.
 
 
 
• **Ciliary Muscles and Suspensory Ligaments**:
 
 
• The lens is held in place by **suspensory ligaments** attached to the **ciliary body**.
 
• The tension in these ligaments changes based on the contraction or relaxation of the **ciliary muscles**, thereby altering the lens shape.
 
 
 
• **Presbyopia**:
 
 
• With **age**, the **power of accommodation** usually decreases as the ciliary muscles weaken and the **crystalline lens** loses its flexibility.
 
• This condition, where people find it difficult to see nearby objects comfortably and distinctly without corrective eye-wear, is called **Presbyopia**.
 
 
 
• **Other Eye Functions**:
 
 
• **Adaptation**: This refers to the ability of the **pupil** and **iris** to adjust to varying levels of **light intensity**.
 
• **Reflection**: This is the bouncing back of light when it hits a surface; it is not the primary mechanism of focusing within the biological lens of the eye.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Image Formation**: The eye lens forms a **real and inverted image** of the object on the **retina**, which is a light-sensitive screen at the back of the eye.
 
• **Refractive Power**: The **cornea** actually performs about **70-80%** of the total **refraction** (focusing) of the eye. The **lens** provides the final, adjustable **20-30%** of the power required for fine-tuning.
 
• **Optical Power Unit**: The power of a lens is measured in **Dioptres (D)**. The accommodation power of a healthy young human eye is approximately **4 Dioptres**.
 
• **Refractive Defects**: When the eye cannot properly accommodate or focus light on the retina, it leads to defects like **Myopia** (nearsightedness), **Hypermetropia** (farsightedness), and **Astigmatism**.
</ul

questions.question: If a particle covers a distance of 12 m in every 3 s, what is the slope of its distance-time graph?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4.0 m/s**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **slope** of a **distance-time graph** is a physical representation of the **speed** of an object. In physics, the slope is defined as the vertical change (rise) divided by the horizontal change (run).
 
• In this specific problem, the particle covers a **distance** of **12 m** in every **3 s**. This indicates that the particle is moving at a **constant rate**, which is a characteristic of **uniform motion**.
 
• To calculate the **slope**, we use the formula: **Slope = Change in Distance / Change in Time**. This is equivalent to the formula for speed: **v = d / t**.
 
• By substituting the given numerical values into the formula: **Slope = 12 m / 3 s**. Performing the division gives a result of **4.0 m/s**.
 
• Since the **slope** is **4.0 m/s**, it tells us that for every **1 second** that passes, the particle moves exactly **4 meters**. The **linear** nature of the graph (a straight line) confirms that the **speed** remains **constant** throughout the motion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Distance-Time Graph Fundamentals:**
 
 
• On a **distance-time graph**, the **time** is always plotted on the **x-axis** (the independent variable), and the **distance** is plotted on the **y-axis** (the dependent variable).
 
• The **unit** for the slope in this graph is **meters per second (m/s)**, which is the standard **SI unit** for **speed**.
 
 
 
• **Types of Motion on Graphs:**
 
 
• **Uniform Motion:** Represented by a **straight line** passing through the origin. The **constant slope** indicates a **constant speed**.
 
• **Non-Uniform Motion:** Represented by a **curved line** (parabola). A curve indicates that the object is **accelerating** or **decelerating**, meaning the **speed** is changing over time.
 
• **Object at Rest:** Represented by a **horizontal line** parallel to the time axis. In this case, the **slope** is **0**, indicating a **speed** of **0 m/s**.
 
 
 
• **Speed vs. Velocity:**
 
 
• While the slope of a **distance-time graph** gives the **speed** (a **scalar quantity**), the slope of a **displacement-time graph** provides the **velocity** (a **vector quantity**).
 
• Speed only considers **magnitude**, whereas velocity considers both **magnitude** and **direction**.
 
 
 
• **Graphical Interpretation:**
 
 
• A **steeper line** on the graph indicates a **higher slope** and thus a **greater speed**. Conversely, a line with a **low angle** of inclination indicates a **slower speed**.
 
• If the line is **vertical**, it would imply **infinite speed** (covering distance in zero time), which is physically impossible for a particle with mass.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The calculation of the slope **12 / 3 = 4** is a direct application of the **rate of change** concept in **kinematics**.
 
• In **calculus** terms, the **speed** is the **first derivative** of **distance** with respect to **time** (**v = dd/dt**). For **linear graphs**, this derivative is simply the **constant slope** of the line.
 
• Understanding **distance-time graphs** is crucial for analyzing **real-world data**, such as the **average speed** of vehicles, **satellite orbits**, or **athletic performance**.
</ul

questions.question: Which factor does NOT increase the rate of evaporation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Decrease in temperature**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Evaporation** is a **surface phenomenon** where liquid molecules gain enough **kinetic energy** to escape into the air as **vapor** at any temperature below the **boiling point**.
 
• An **Increase in surface area** significantly enhances the rate of evaporation because more molecules are exposed to the atmosphere at the **liquid-air interface**. For example, spreading out wet clothes allows them to dry faster. *Since this increases the rate, statement 1 is not the correct factor for this question.*
 
• An **Increase in wind speed** helps in moving the **water vapor** particles away from the surface of the liquid, thereby reducing the **concentration of vapor** in the immediate surroundings and allowing more molecules to escape. *Since this increases the rate, statement 2 is not the correct factor for this question.*
 
• A **Decrease in temperature** results in lower **kinetic energy** for the liquid particles, making it harder for them to overcome the **intermolecular forces** and escape the surface. This directly leads to a slower evaporation process. *Hence, statement 3 is correct as it does NOT increase the rate of evaporation.*
 
• A **Decrease in humidity** increases the rate of evaporation because **dry air** has a higher capacity to absorb moisture than moist air. When the **moisture content** in the air is low, the gradient for evaporation is steeper. *Since this increases the rate, statement 4 is not the correct factor for this question.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Temperature:** The rate of evaporation is **directly proportional** to the **absolute temperature**. Higher temperatures provide the **latent heat of vaporization** required for phase change.
 
• **Humidity:** This is the measure of **water vapor** present in the air at a given **temperature**. On a **rainy day**, when **humidity** is near **100%**, the rate of evaporation is at its lowest, which is why clothes take longer to dry.
 
• **Latent Heat:** During evaporation, the liquid absorbs **energy** from the surroundings to change into a **gas**. This is why evaporation always leads to a **cooling effect** on the remaining liquid or the surface.
 
• **Nature of Liquid:** Different liquids have different **intermolecular forces**. Volatile liquids like **acetone** or **petrol** evaporate much faster than **water** at **25 degrees Celsius** because they have weaker bonds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Bulk vs. Surface Phenomenon:** Unlike **boiling**, which is a **bulk phenomenon** where the entire mass of the liquid reaches the **boiling point**, evaporation occurs only at the **surface**.
 
• **Cooling Applications:** The principle of evaporation is used in **desert coolers** and **earthen pots (Matkas)**. In a **desert cooler**, the evaporation of water absorbs heat from the air, providing a cool breeze during **hot and dry summer** months.
 
• **Atmospheric Pressure:** While not mentioned in the options, a **decrease in atmospheric pressure** also increases the rate of evaporation, as there is less pressure pushing down on the surface to prevent molecules from escaping.
</ul

questions.question: When the distance–time graph of an object is a curved line, it indicates that _________.

options.text: The object is moving with a constant speed
There is no acceleration in the motion
The speed of the object is changing with time

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The speed of the object is changing with time**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a **distance–time graph**, the **time** is typically plotted on the **x-axis** and the **distance** covered by the object is plotted on the **y-axis**.
 
• The **slope** (or **gradient**) of a distance–time graph represents the **speed** of the object. If the graph is a **straight line**, the **slope** is constant, indicating that the object is moving with a **constant speed**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• When the graph is a **curved line**, it implies that the **slope** of the graph is changing at different points in **time**. Since the **slope** represents **speed**, a changing **slope** means the **speed of the object is changing**. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• A change in **speed** over **time** is defined as **acceleration** (or **deceleration**). If the graph is curved, it indicates that the motion is **accelerated**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• If an object remains **stationary**, its **distance** does not change as **time** passes. This would result in a **horizontal straight line** parallel to the **time axis**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Uniform Motion**:
 
 
• An object is said to be in **uniform motion** when it covers **equal distances in equal intervals of time**.
 
• The **distance–time graph** for **uniform motion** is always a **straight line** passing through the origin (if starting from **zero distance**).
 
• In this case, the **acceleration** of the object is **zero**.
 
 
 
• **Non-Uniform Motion**:
 
 
• An object is in **non-uniform motion** when it covers **unequal distances in equal intervals of time**.
 
• The **distance–time graph** for this motion is a **curve**, such as a **parabola**, which indicates that the **speed** is either increasing or decreasing.
 
• **Non-uniform motion** is also referred to as **accelerated motion**.
 
 
 
• **Instantaneous Speed**:
 
 
• On a **curved distance–time graph**, the **speed** at any particular **instant** can be found by drawing a **tangent** to the curve at that point and calculating its **slope**.
 
• The **steeper** the curve, the **higher** the **instantaneous speed** of the object at that **time**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **SI unit** of **speed** is **meters per second (m/s)**, while **time** is measured in **seconds (s)** and **distance** in **meters (m)**.
 
• A **distance–time graph** can never go **downwards** because **distance** is a **scalar quantity** and can only **increase** or stay **constant** with **time**; it can never be **negative**.
 
• If the curve bends **upwards** (getting steeper), the object is **speeding up** (**positive acceleration**).
 
• If the curve starts to **level off** (getting flatter), the object is **slowing down** (**negative acceleration** or **deceleration**).

questions.question: A plant breeder crosses two pure-breeding pea plants—one producing round seeds and the other producing wrinkled seeds. Based on Mendel’s findings, what phenotype would all the seeds in the F₁ generation display?

options.text: A mix of round and wrinkled in varying proportions

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Round seeds**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gregor Mendel**, often referred to as the **Father of Genetics**, conducted his primary experiments using **Pisum sativum** (the **garden pea plant**) in the **19th century**.
 
• In this specific experiment, **seed shape** is the trait under observation. Mendel identified **round seeds** as the **dominant trait** and **wrinkled seeds** as the **recessive trait**.
 
• A **pure-breeding** plant is **homozygous**, meaning it carries two identical **alleles** for a gene. The **pure-breeding round plant** has the genotype **RR**, while the **pure-breeding wrinkled plant** has the genotype **rr**.
 
• When these two are crossed, the **F1 generation** (first filial generation) receives one **allele** from each parent, resulting in a **heterozygous genotype** of **Rr**.
 
• According to **Mendel’s Law of Dominance**, in a **heterozygous** individual, the **dominant allele** (R) completely masks the expression of the **recessive allele** (r).
 
• Consequently, every single seed produced in the **F1 generation** will exhibit the **round phenotype**, even though they carry the hidden gene for wrinkled seeds. ***Hence, the correct answer is Round seeds.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mendelian Inheritance Patterns**:
 
 
• **Monohybrid Cross**: The cross mentioned is a **monohybrid cross** because it focuses on a **single trait** (seed shape). Mendel performed these crosses for **seven different traits** including plant height, flower color, and pod shape.
 
• **F2 Generation**: When **F1 plants** (Rr) are **self-pollinated**, they produce the **F2 generation**. In this stage, the **recessive trait** (wrinkled) reappears in a specific **phenotypic ratio** of **3:1** (3 round to 1 wrinkled).
 
 
 
• **Key Genetic Terminology**:
 
 
• **Genotype**: This refers to the **genetic makeup** of the organism (e.g., **RR, Rr, or rr**).
 
• **Phenotype**: This refers to the **observable physical characteristics** of the organism (e.g., **round or wrinkled**).
 
• **Law of Segregation**: This law states that during the formation of **gametes**, the **alleles** for each gene **segregate** from each other so that each gamete carries only **one allele** for each gene.
 
 
 
• **Experimental Data**:
 
 
• In his **1865** paper, Mendel reported that out of **7,324** seeds in the **F2 generation**, **5,474** were round and **1,850** were wrinkled, which closely approximates the **3:1 ratio**.
 
• The **genotypic ratio** of the **F2 generation** is **1:2:1**, representing one **homozygous dominant** (RR), two **heterozygous** (Rr), and one **homozygous recessive** (rr).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Seven Traits Studied by Mendel**:
 
 
• **Seed Shape**: Round (Dominant) vs. Wrinkled (Recessive).
 
• **Seed Color**: Yellow (Dominant) vs. Green (Recessive).
 
• **Flower Color**: Violet (Dominant) vs. White (Recessive).
 
• **Pod Shape**: Inflated (Dominant) vs. Constricted (Recessive).
 
• **Pod Color**: Green (Dominant) vs. Yellow (Recessive).
 
• **Flower Position**: Axial (Dominant) vs. Terminal (Recessive).
 
• **Stem Height**: Tall (Dominant) vs. Dwarf (Recessive).
 
 
 
• **Punnett Square Analysis**:
 
 
• The **Punnett Square** for the **F1 cross** involves a **2x2 grid**. If we place the **R** and **R** gametes from the round parent on one side and **r** and **r** from the wrinkled parent on the other, all four squares result in the **Rr** genotype.

questions.question: When copper reacts with oxygen on heating in air, which of the following correctly represents the product formed, along with its colour?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Copper(II) oxide (CuO) – black in colour**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When **copper metal** is heated in the presence of **oxygen** (air), a **chemical reaction** occurs where the copper atoms combine with oxygen atoms to form a new compound.
 
• The product formed is **Copper(II) oxide**, which has the chemical formula **CuO**. In this compound, the **oxidation state** of copper is **+2**.
 
• The surface of the **reddish-brown copper metal** becomes coated with a **black-coloured layer** during this process. This change in color is a clear indicator of a **chemical change**.
 
• The balanced **chemical equation** for this reaction is: **2Cu + O2 → 2CuO** (upon **heating**).
 
• This reaction is classified as an **oxidation reaction** because copper **gains oxygen** to form its oxide. It is also a **combination reaction** as two reactants combine to form a single product.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Copper(I) oxide (Cu2O):** This is another oxide of copper where the **oxidation state** of copper is **+1**. It is typically **red** or **brownish-red** in colour. While it can be formed under specific conditions, the primary product of heating copper in excess air is the **black Copper(II) oxide**.
 
• **Reactivity of Copper:** Copper is a **transition metal** located in **Group 11** of the **Periodic Table**. It is relatively **low in the reactivity series**, meaning it does not react with oxygen at **room temperature**, but requires **high temperatures** to undergo significant oxidation.
 
• **Basic Nature:** **Copper(II) oxide** is a **basic oxide**. When it reacts with **dilute acids** like **hydrochloric acid (HCl)**, it forms **copper salts** (like copper chloride) and **water**.
 
• **Difference from Corrosion:** The **black coating** formed by heating is different from the **greenish patina** seen on copper structures (like the Statue of Liberty) over long periods. That green layer is **basic copper carbonate**, formed by the slow reaction of copper with **moist carbon dioxide** and **oxygen** in the atmosphere at **ambient temperatures**.
 
• **Industrial Uses:** **Copper(II) oxide** is used as a **pigment** in ceramics to produce blue, red, and green (and sometimes gray, pink, or black) glazes. It is also used as a **catalyst** in various chemical reactions and in the production of **wood preservatives**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Reduction of CuO:** If **hydrogen gas** is passed over the **heated black Copper(II) oxide**, the black coating turns **brown** again as the oxygen is removed, regenerating **metallic copper**. This is a **redox reaction**: **CuO + H2 → Cu + H2O**.
 
• **Physical Properties:** **Copper(II) oxide** is a **solid** at room temperature and is **insoluble in water**. It has a **monoclinic crystal structure** and is often found in nature as the mineral **tenorite**.
 
• **Safety:** While copper is an essential trace element for humans, **Copper(II) oxide** can be **toxic** if inhaled or ingested in large quantities, as it acts as an **irritant** to the respiratory tract and gastrointestinal system.

questions.question: Which of the following is the energy possessed by a body by virtue of its position, shape and configuration?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Potential Energy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Potential Energy** is defined as the energy stored in an object or a system due to its **position**, **shape**, or **configuration**. It is "potential" because it has the capacity to do work when the state of the object changes.
 
• There are various forms of potential energy, the most common being **Gravitational Potential Energy**. This depends on an object's **mass**, its **height** relative to a reference point, and the **acceleration due to gravity**. The mathematical expression is **P.E. = mgh**.
 
• Another significant form is **Elastic Potential Energy**, which is the energy stored in objects that can be **compressed or stretched**, such as a **coiled spring**, a **stretched rubber band**, or a **drawn archer's bow**. This energy is a result of the change in the **configuration** or **shape** of the object.
 
• Potential energy can also be **Chemical** (stored in bonds), **Electrical**, or **Magnetic**, all depending on the **relative arrangement** of parts within a system.
 
• Because it represents the energy of an object based on its state of rest and arrangement rather than its motion, it perfectly matches the definition provided in the question. ***Hence, the correct answer is Potential Energy.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kinetic Energy**: 
 
 
• This is the energy possessed by an object by virtue of its **motion**. 
 
• Unlike potential energy, which is based on position, kinetic energy depends on the **mass** and the **square of the velocity** of the object (**K.E. = 1/2 mv²**). 
 
• Examples include a **speeding car**, a **flowing river**, or a **falling stone**. *Hence, this option is incorrect as it relates to motion, not position.*
 
 
 
• **Heat Energy**: 
 
 
• Also known as **thermal energy**, it is the internal energy of a system resulting from the **microscopic motion** (vibration and collision) of **atoms and molecules**. 
 
• It flows from a body at a **higher temperature** to one at a **lower temperature**. 
 
• It is typically measured in **Joules** or **Calories**. *Hence, this option is incorrect as it refers to internal molecular kinetic energy.*
 
 
 
• **Muscular Energy**: 
 
 
• This is the energy derived from the **metabolic processes** within the **muscles** of living organisms. 
 
• It allows animals and humans to perform **physical work**, such as **lifting weights**, **walking**, or **running**. 
 
• It is a transformation of **chemical energy** obtained from food into **mechanical energy**. *Hence, this option is incorrect as it is a biological energy source for activity.*
 
 
 
• **Mechanical Energy**:
 
 
• The **sum total** of potential energy and kinetic energy in a system is called **Mechanical Energy**. 
 
• According to the **Law of Conservation of Energy**, in an isolated system, energy can neither be created nor destroyed; it only **transforms** from one form (like potential) to another (like kinetic).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **S.I. Unit** of energy (both Kinetic and Potential) is the **Joule (J)**, named after the physicist **James Prescott Joule**.
 
• Energy is a **scalar quantity**, meaning it has **magnitude** but no **direction**.
 
• The **Commercial Unit** of energy is the **kilowatt-hour (kWh)**, which is commonly used for **electricity billing** and is equal to **3.6 million Joules**.
 
• A **stretched bow** possesses **Elastic Potential Energy** because of its **shape/configuration**; as soon as the arrow is released, this energy converts into the **Kinetic Energy** of the arrow.

questions.question: The common name for *Apis florae* is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The little bee**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Migration:** **Apis florea** is highly **migratory** and often shifts its colony location based on **seasonal changes** and the availability of **floral nectar**.

questions.question: When the frequency of vibration of a sound source increases, the resulting sound will have _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Higher pitch**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **pitch** of a sound is directly determined by its **frequency of vibration**. When the frequency of vibration of a sound source **increases**, the resulting sound will have a **higher pitch**.
 
• **Frequency** is defined as the **number of oscillations** or vibrations per unit of time (usually one second). It is measured in **Hertz (Hz)**.
 
• A **high-frequency** vibration produces a sound that is **shrill** and has a high pitch, such as the sound of a **whistle** or a **bird chirping**.
 
• Conversely, a **low-frequency** vibration results in a sound with a **lower pitch**, such as the beating of a **drum** or the **roar of a lion**.
 
• It is important to note that **pitch** is a subjective perception of the frequency of sound waves by the human ear, whereas **frequency** is a physical, measurable quantity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Amplitude and Loudness:**
 
 
• The **loudness** of a sound depends on the **amplitude** of the vibration. **Loudness** is proportional to the **square of the amplitude** of the vibration producing the sound.
 
• If the **amplitude** is large, the sound produced is **loud**; if the amplitude is small, the sound is **feeble**. Therefore, increasing frequency does not necessarily increase loudness.
 
 
 
• **Human Audibility Range:**
 
 
• The human ear can typically hear sounds with frequencies ranging from **20 Hz to 20,000 Hz** (20 kHz).
 
• Sounds with a **frequency** below **20 Hz** are termed **infrasonic**, while those above **20,000 Hz** are termed **ultrasonic**.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Sound Waves:**
 
 
• **Wavelength:** The distance between two consecutive compressions or rarefactions in a sound wave.
 
• **Time Period:** The time taken by the wave to complete one full **oscillation**. It is the reciprocal of **frequency** (T = 1/f).
 
• **Speed of Sound:** The distance a point on the wave travels per unit time. In **dry air** at **20 degrees Celsius**, the speed of sound is approximately **343 meters per second**.
 
 
 
• **Unit of Loudness:**
 
 
• The loudness of sound is measured in **decibels (dB)**. Normal conversation is typically around **60 dB**, while sounds above **80 dB** can become physically painful or harmful to the human ear over time.
 
 
 
• **Quality (Timbre):**
 
 
• This is the characteristic of sound that allows us to distinguish between two sounds of the same **pitch** and **loudness**, such as different musical instruments or human voices.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• In general, the **voice of a woman** has a **higher frequency** and is **shriller** than that of a man, meaning it has a **higher pitch**.
 
• The **voice of a man** typically has a **lower frequency** of vibration, resulting in a **lower pitch** or deeper voice.
 
• This difference is primarily due to the **length and thickness** of the **vocal cords**; men usually have longer vocal cords (about **20 mm**) compared to women (about **15 mm**).
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following correctly represents the mass number of an element?

options.text: The sum of protons and neutrons
The difference between protons and neutrons

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The sum of protons and neutrons**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **mass number** (represented by the symbol **A**) of an element is defined as the total count of **protons** and **neutrons** present in the **nucleus** of an atom.
 
• Protons and neutrons are collectively referred to as **nucleons** because they occupy the central core of the atom.
 
• The mathematical representation of the mass number is **A = Z + n**, where **Z** represents the **atomic number** (the number of **protons**) and **n** represents the **number of neutrons**.
 
• Since **electrons** have a negligible mass (approximately **1/1840** of the mass of a proton), they are not included in the calculation of the **mass number**.
 
• For example, an atom of **Aluminum** has **13 protons** and **14 neutrons**; therefore, its **mass number** is **27**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Atomic Number (Z):**
 
 
• This refers strictly to the number of **protons** in the nucleus of an atom. It defines the identity of the element and its position in the **Modern Periodic Table**.
 
• In a **neutral atom**, the number of **protons** is exactly equal to the number of **electrons**.
 
 
 
• **Isotopes:**
 
 
• These are atoms of the **same element** that possess the same **atomic number** but different **mass numbers**.
 
• This variation occurs because **isotopes** have the same number of **protons** but a different number of **neutrons**.
 
• **Example:** Carbon has isotopes like **Carbon-12** (6 protons, 6 neutrons) and **Carbon-14** (6 protons, 8 neutrons), the latter of which is used in **radiocarbon dating**.
 
 
 
• **Isobars:**
 
 
• These are atoms of **different chemical elements** that have the same **mass number** but different **atomic numbers**.
 
• **Example:** **Argon-40** and **Calcium-40** both have a mass number of **40**, despite having **18** and **20** protons respectively.
 
 
 
• **Relative Atomic Mass:**
 
 
• Unlike the **mass number** (which is always a whole number), **relative atomic mass** is often a decimal because it is a weighted average of all the naturally occurring **isotopes** of that element.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The discovery of the **neutron** by **James Chadwick** in **1932** was crucial for the accurate determination of **mass numbers**.
 
• The **mass number** is typically written as a **superscript** to the left of the chemical symbol (e.g., **12C**), while the **atomic number** is written as a **subscript** (e.g., **6C**).
 
• The **nucleus** contains nearly **99.9%** of the total mass of the atom, concentrated in an extremely small volume compared to the total size of the atom, a fact first proposed by **Ernest Rutherford** in **1911**.
 
• The **stability** of a nucleus is often determined by the **neutron-to-proton ratio** (n/p ratio); if this ratio is too high or too low, the atom may become **radioactive**.
</ul

questions.question:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are true about the buoyant force experienced by an object when it is immersed in a fluid?

(i) All objects experience a force of buoyancy when they are immersed in a fluid.
(ii) The magnitude of this buoyant force depends on the density of the fluid.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both (i) and (ii)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Buoyant force**, also known as **upthrust**, is the upward force exerted by a **fluid** (liquid or gas) that opposes the **weight** of an object immersed in it.
 
• All objects, regardless of their **material**, **mass**, or **shape**, experience a force of **buoyancy** when they are partially or fully immersed in a fluid. This force acts in the **upward direction**, contrary to the force of **gravity**. ***Hence, statement (i) is correct.***
 
• The magnitude of the **buoyant force** is determined by the formula **Fb = ρVg**, where **ρ** (rho) represents the **density** of the fluid. Because the force is directly proportional to the **density** of the medium, an object will experience a greater upward force in a denser fluid (like **saltwater**) compared to a less dense fluid (like **freshwater**). ***Hence, statement (ii) is correct.***
 
• According to **Archimedes' Principle**, the magnitude of the **buoyant force** is exactly equal to the **weight of the fluid displaced** by the body.
 
• The point at which the **buoyant force** acts on the body is called the **centre of buoyancy**, which coincides with the **centre of gravity** of the displaced fluid.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Both (i) and (ii).***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Archimedes' Principle:**
 
 
• This fundamental law of **physics** was discovered by the **Greek** mathematician **Archimedes** in the **3rd century BC**.
 
• It explains why some objects **float** while others **sink**. If the **buoyant force** is equal to or greater than the **weight** of the object, the object will **float**; otherwise, it will **sink**.
 
 
 
• **Density and Buoyancy:**
 
 
• The **density** of a substance is its **mass per unit volume**. The **SI unit** for density is **kg/m³**.
 
• Pure **water** has a density of approximately **1000 kg/m³** at **4°C**. **Mercury**, being much denser at **13,600 kg/m³**, exerts a significantly higher **buoyant force** on objects.
 
 
 
• **Practical Applications:**
 
 
• **Ship Design:** Large ships made of **steel** float because they are designed to displace a **volume of water** whose weight is equal to the weight of the ship.
 
• **Lactometers:** These are instruments used to determine the **purity** of a sample of **milk** based on the principle of **buoyancy**.
 
• **Hydrometers:** These are used for determining the **density of liquids** by measuring how deep they sink in a fluid.
 
• **Hot Air Balloons:** They rise because the **hot air** inside the balloon is less dense than the surrounding **cool air**, creating a net upward **buoyant force**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Factors affecting Buoyant Force:**
 
 
• **Volume of the immersed object:** The larger the **volume** of the object submerged, the greater the **buoyant force** it experiences.
 
• **Density of the fluid:** As established, higher **fluid density** leads to a stronger **upthrust**.
 
• **Acceleration due to gravity (g):** In a **zero-gravity** environment (like **free fall** or **outer space**), the **buoyant force** becomes **zero**. On **Earth**, **g** is approximately **9.8 m/s²**.
 
 
 
• **Apparent Weight:**
 
 
• When an object is immersed in a **fluid**, it appears to lose **weight**. This **apparent weight** is equal to the **actual weight** of the object minus the **buoyant force**.
 
• This phenomenon is why it is easier to lift a heavy **stone** while it is still under **water** than to lift it once it reaches the **surface**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following correctly represents the pathway of air during respiration in human beings?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nostrils → Throat → Lungs → Alveoli**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The respiratory system in human beings is responsible for the exchange of gases, primarily **Oxygen (O2)** and **Carbon Dioxide (CO2)**, between the body and the environment.
 
• Air enters the body through the **Nostrils**, where it is filtered by fine **hairs** and **mucus** to remove dust and foreign particles.
 
• From the nostrils, the air passes through the **Nasal Passage** into the **Throat** (which includes the **Pharynx** and **Larynx**). The **Pharynx** serves as a common passage for both food and air.
 
• The air then travels down the **Trachea** (windpipe) and enters the **Lungs** through the **Bronchi** and **Bronchioles**.
 
• The final destination of the inhaled air is the **Alveoli**, which are tiny balloon-like structures where the actual **gas exchange** takes place with the blood **capillaries**.
 
• Option 1 suggests air goes through the **Food pipe** and **Heart**. The food pipe (**Oesophagus**) belongs to the digestive system, and the heart is part of the circulatory system. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• Option 2 correctly describes the flow from **Nostrils** to the **Throat**, then into the **Lungs**, and finally reaching the **Alveoli**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• Option 3 mentions the **Stomach**, which is a major organ of the **Digestive System** and not involved in the air pathway. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• Option 4 mentions the **Heart** as a pathway for air, which is false, as the heart pumps blood, not air. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pharynx and Larynx:** The **Pharynx** leads to the **Larynx** (voice box). A muscular flap called the **Epiglottis** covers the opening of the **Glottis** during swallowing to prevent food from entering the windpipe.
 
• **Trachea (Windpipe):** It is a tube supported by **C-shaped cartilaginous rings**. These rings ensure that the air passage does not **collapse** even when there is little air in it.
 
• **The Bronchial Tree:** Inside the lungs, the **Trachea** divides into **Primary Bronchi** (right and left), which further branch into **Secondary** and **Tertiary Bronchi**, and eventually into thin **Bronchioles**.
 
• **Mechanism of Alveoli:** The **Alveoli** provide a very large **surface area** (approximately **80 to 100 square meters** in an adult) for the diffusion of gases. The walls of the alveoli are extremely thin and surrounded by a vast network of **blood vessels**.
 
• **Diaphragm:** It is a large, **dome-shaped muscle** located at the base of the chest cavity. Its **contraction** increases the chest cavity volume, creating a vacuum that pulls air into the lungs (**Inhalation**).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Breathing vs. Respiration:** **Breathing** is the physical process of **Inhalation** and **Exhalation**, whereas **Respiration** is a biochemical process where **Glucose** is broken down in cells to release **Energy** (ATP).
 
• **Transport of Gases:** **Haemoglobin**, the red pigment in **Red Blood Cells (RBCs)**, has a high affinity for **Oxygen** and carries it from the lungs to the tissues. **Carbon Dioxide** is more soluble in water and is mostly transported in the **dissolved form** in the blood **plasma**.
 
• **Diffusion:** The exchange of gases at the alveolar site occurs through **Simple Diffusion** based on the **pressure gradient** or concentration gradient of the gases.
 
• **Residual Volume:** Even after forceful expiration, some amount of air always remains in the lungs, known as the **Residual Volume**, to ensure there is sufficient time for **Oxygen** to be absorbed.

questions.question: Metals are generally good conductors of heat. Which of the following is an exception to this?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mercury**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Metals are typically characterized by their high **thermal conductivity** and **electrical conductivity** due to the presence of **free electrons** that can move easily through the **atomic lattice**.
 
• **Mercury (Hg)** is a notable exception to this trend as it is a **poor conductor of heat** compared to most other metals. ***Hence, option 1 is correct.***
 
• **Mercury** is the only metal that exists in a **liquid state** at **room temperature** (approximately **25°C**), which significantly influences its physical and thermal properties.
 
• **Iron (Fe)** is a **good conductor** of heat and is widely used in **industrial machinery** and **construction** due to its durability and thermal properties. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Aluminium (Al)** is an **excellent conductor** of heat, which is why it is extensively used in **kitchen utensils** and **heat sinks** for electronic components. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Copper (Cu)** is one of the **best thermal conductors** among common metals, second only to silver, making it the primary choice for **heat exchangers** and **electrical wiring**. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Thermal Conductivity**: This is a **physical property** of a material that defines its ability to **transfer heat**. In metals, heat is transferred via **lattice vibrations** (phonons) and the **kinetic energy** of **free-moving electrons**.
 
• **Mercury (Hg)**: With an **atomic number** of **80**, it is used in **thermometers**, **barometers**, and **fluorescent lamps**. Despite being a poor heat conductor, its **uniform coefficient of thermal expansion** makes it ideal for measuring temperature.
 
• **Lead (Pb)**: Along with Mercury, **Lead** is also considered a **poor conductor of heat** among the metal group. It is commonly used for **radiation shielding** and in **lead-acid batteries**.
 
• **Best Conductors**: **Silver (Ag)** is the **most efficient conductor** of both heat and electricity, followed by **Copper (Cu)** and **Gold (Au)**.
 
• **Metals in Periodic Table**: Most metals are located on the **left side** and in the **center** of the **Periodic Table**, categorized as **Alkali metals**, **Alkaline earth metals**, **Transition metals**, and **Post-transition metals**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Malleability and Ductility**: Metals are generally **malleable** (can be beaten into **thin sheets**) and **ductile** (can be drawn into **thin wires**). **Gold** is the most **malleable** metal known to man.
 
• **Sonority**: Metals are **sonorous**, meaning they produce a **distinct ringing sound** when struck. This property is utilized in the manufacturing of **musical instruments** and **bells**.
 
• **Metallic Lustre**: Metals possess a **shiny surface** in their pure state, a quality known as **lustre**. This is due to the **reflection of light** by the **delocalized electrons** on the surface.
 
• **Hardness**: While most metals are **physically hard**, elements like **Sodium (Na)** and **Potassium (K)** are soft enough to be **sliced with a knife**.
 
• **Melting and Boiling Points**: Metals typically have **high melting and boiling points**. **Tungsten (W)** has the **highest melting point**, making it suitable for **light bulb filaments**.
</ul

questions.question: Which process occurring in the Golgi apparatus shows its role in synthesis?

options.text: Synthesis of nucleic acids from ribosomes
Formation of complex sugars from simple sugars
Conversion of proteins into amino acids

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Formation of complex sugars from simple sugars**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Golgi apparatus**, also known as the **Golgi complex** or **Golgi body**, plays a crucial role in the **biosynthesis** of various cellular components, specifically in the **formation of complex sugars from simple sugars**.
 
• In many cases, the **Golgi apparatus** is involved in the modification of **proteins** and **lipids** by adding **sugar** moieties, a process known as **glycosylation**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• The **synthesis of nucleic acids** (DNA and RNA) occurs in the **nucleus**, **mitochondria**, and **chloroplasts**, while **ribosomes** are the site for **protein synthesis**, not nucleic acid synthesis. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The **absorption of water through osmosis** is a **physical process** regulated by the **plasma membrane** and **tonoplast** (vacuolar membrane), and is not a synthetic role attributed to the **Golgi apparatus**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The **conversion of proteins into amino acids** is a **catabolic** or degradative process (proteolysis) that typically occurs in the **lysosomes** or through **proteasomes**, rather than being a function of synthesis in the Golgi. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• The **Golgi apparatus** acts as a dispatch station, where products of the **Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER)** are **modified**, **packaged**, and **sorted** for delivery to their destinations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Discovery and Structure**:
 
 
• The **Golgi apparatus** was first identified by the **Italian** biologist **Camillo Golgi** in **1898** using a silver staining technique.
 
• It consists of a series of flattened, membrane-bound sacs called **cisternae**, which are typically stacked together in **4 to 8** layers.
 
• The structure has a distinct **polarity**, featuring a **cis face** (entry face near the ER) and a **trans face** (exit face near the plasma membrane).
 
 
 
• **Primary Functions**:
 
 
• **Storage and Packaging**: It stores **proteins** and **lipids** synthesized in the **Endoplasmic Reticulum** and packages them into **vesicles** for **secretion**.
 
• **Modification**: It modifies **glycoproteins** and **glycolipids** by trimming or adding specific **sugar** molecules.
 
• **Lysosome Formation**: The **Golgi apparatus** is directly involved in the production of **lysosomes**, which contain **hydrolytic enzymes** for intracellular digestion.
 
 
 
• **Golgi in Plant Cells**:
 
 
• In **plant cells**, the Golgi bodies are often scattered and are referred to as **dictyosomes**.
 
• They play a vital role in synthesizing **complex polysaccharides** like **pectin** and **hemicellulose**, which are essential components of the **cell wall**.
 
 
 
• **Vesicular Transport**:
 
 
• **Transport vesicles** from the **ER** fuse with the **cis-Golgi**, and after processing, **secretory vesicles** bud off from the **trans-Golgi** to move toward the **cell surface** or other **organelles**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following is true for mitosis but not for meiosis?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Produces identical daughter cells**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mitosis** is a process of **cell division** where a single cell divides into two **genetically identical daughter cells**. The primary purpose of mitosis is for **growth** and to replace worn-out cells.
 
• In **Mitosis**, the **chromosomal number** remains the same as that of the parent cell, which is why it is often referred to as **equational division**. This ensures that each daughter cell receives a complete and **identical set of DNA**. ***Hence, the statement "Produces identical daughter cells" is true for mitosis.***
 
• **Meiosis**, on the other hand, is a specialized form of cell division that reduces the **chromosome number** by half, resulting in the production of **haploid cells** (gametes). These daughter cells are **genetically distinct** from the parent and each other. ***Hence, the statement "Results in haploid cells" is true for meiosis, not mitosis.***
 
• **Genetic variation** is a hallmark of **Meiosis** due to processes like **crossing over** and **independent assortment** during **Prophase I**. Mitosis does not typically promote variation as it aims to produce **clones**. ***Hence, the statement "Promotes genetic variation" is true for meiosis, not mitosis.***
 
• **Mitosis** occurs in **somatic cells** (all body cells except reproductive ones), whereas **Meiosis** occurs specifically in **reproductive cells** (germ cells) to produce sperm and eggs. ***Hence, the statement "Occurs in reproductive cells" is true for meiosis, not mitosis.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Stages of Mitosis:**
 
 
• **Prophase**: The **chromatin** condenses into visible **chromosomes**, and the **nuclear envelope** begins to break down.
 
• **Metaphase**: Chromosomes align at the **metaphase plate** (the cell's equator) to ensure even distribution.
 
• **Anaphase**: **Sister chromatids** are pulled apart toward opposite **poles** of the cell.
 
• **Telophase**: Two new **nuclear envelopes** form around the separated sets of chromosomes, followed by **cytokinesis** (division of the cytoplasm).
 
 
 
• **Key Differences in Meiosis:**
 
 
• Meiosis involves two successive rounds of division: **Meiosis I** and **Meiosis II**.
 
• During **Meiosis I**, **homologous chromosomes** pair up and exchange genetic material, a process known as **recombination** or **crossing over**.
 
• The end result of meiosis is **four daughter cells**, each containing a **haploid (n)** number of chromosomes, compared to the **diploid (2n)** nature of the parent cell.
 
 
 
• **Biological Significance:**
 
 
• **Mitosis** is essential for **asexual reproduction** in single-celled organisms and for **tissue repair** and **development** in multicellular organisms.
 
• **Meiosis** is critical for **sexual reproduction**, as it maintains the constant **chromosome number** across generations and increases **biodiversity** within a population.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Somatic Cells vs. Germ Cells**: **Somatic cells** make up the bulk of an organism's body (e.g., skin, muscle, bone) and divide via **mitosis**. **Germ cells** are located in the **gonads** (testes and ovaries) and undergo **meiosis** to produce **gametes**.
 
• **DNA Replication**: In both mitosis and meiosis, **DNA replication** occurs only once during the **S-phase** of the **interphase** preceding the division.
 
• **Ploidy**: Mitosis maintains **ploidy** (e.g., **2n to 2n**), while meiosis reduces **ploidy** (e.g., **2n to n**).
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following is a heterogeneous mixture?
questions.solution:
p data-end="57" data-start="0">The correct answer is __**Sand and water**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **heterogeneous mixture** is a type of mixture in which the components are **not uniformly distributed** throughout the volume and exist in **distinct phases**.
 
• **Sand and water** is a **heterogeneous mixture** because the sand particles do not dissolve in water. Instead, they remain suspended for a while and eventually settle at the bottom due to **gravity**, a process known as **sedimentation**. ***Hence, option 4 is the correct answer.***
 
• **Sugar solution** is a **homogeneous mixture** (specifically a **true solution**) because the sugar molecules are distributed **uniformly** among the water molecules, and the mixture has a consistent composition throughout. ***Hence, option 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Salt solution** is also a **homogeneous mixture**. Once **Sodium Chloride (NaCl)** is dissolved in water, the individual ions are spread evenly, making it impossible to distinguish the salt from the water by simple observation. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Air** is considered a **homogeneous mixture** of various gases, primarily **Nitrogen (78%)** and **Oxygen (21%)**, along with small amounts of **Argon**, **Carbon dioxide**, and water vapor. Under normal conditions, these gases are mixed thoroughly at the molecular level. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Classification of Matter**: Matter is generally classified into **pure substances** (elements and compounds) and **mixtures**. Mixtures are further divided into **homogeneous** and **heterogeneous** categories based on the uniformity of their composition.
 
• **Homogeneous Mixtures**: 
 
 
• These possess a **single phase**.
 
• The particle size is typically less than **1 nanometer**.
 
• They do not scatter a beam of light (no **Tyndall effect**).
 
• Examples include **alloys** (like **Brass**), **vinegar**, and **tap water**.
 
 
 
• **Heterogeneous Mixtures**:
 
 
• These consist of **two or more phases**.
 
• They include **suspensions** (large particles that settle) and **colloids** (smaller particles that stay dispersed).
 
• **Suspensions** have particle sizes larger than **1000 nanometers**.
 
• Examples include **oil and water**, **mixture of iron filings and sulfur**, and **muddy water**.
 
 
 
• **Physical Separation**: Components of a heterogeneous mixture can usually be separated using **physical methods** such as **filtration**, **decantation**, **centrifugation**, or **manual picking**. For **sand and water**, **filtration** is a highly effective method to recover the solid sand.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Colloids**: While they may appear homogeneous to the naked eye (like **milk** or **blood**), they are technically **heterogeneous** when viewed under an ultra-microscope because the particles are not truly dissolved.
 
• **Solubility**: The nature of the mixture (homogeneous vs. heterogeneous) often depends on the **solubility** of the solute in the solvent. **Sand** (silicon dioxide) is insoluble in water, leading to a heterogeneous result, whereas **sugar** is highly soluble.
 
• **Proportions**: Unlike **compounds**, which have a fixed chemical ratio, mixtures can be prepared in **any proportion**. You can have a mixture of **1 gram** of sand in **1 liter** of water or **100 grams**; both remain heterogeneous.
</ul

questions.question: Which rule helps in identifying the direction of the force acting on a current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fleming’s left-hand rule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fleming’s left-hand rule** is specifically used to determine the direction of the **mechanical force** (or motion) acting on a **current-carrying conductor** when it is placed in an external **magnetic field**.
 
• According to this rule, if we stretch the **thumb**, the **forefinger**, and the **middle finger** of the **left hand** such that they are **mutually perpendicular** to each other, each finger represents a specific vector.
 
• The **Forefinger** points in the direction of the **Magnetic Field** (from North to South pole).
 
• The **Middle finger** points in the direction of the **Electric Current** (flowing through the conductor).
 
• The **Thumb** then points in the direction of the **Force** or the **Motion** of the conductor. ***Hence, the correct answer is Fleming’s left-hand rule.***
 
• This principle is the fundamental working basis of an **Electric Motor**, where electrical energy is converted into **mechanical energy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ohm’s Law**:
 
 
• Formulated by **Georg Simon Ohm** in **1827**, it states that the **current** passing through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the **voltage** across the two points, provided physical conditions remain constant.
 
• The formula is **V = IR**, where **V** is voltage, **I** is current, and **R** is **resistance**. It does not determine the direction of force in magnetic fields.
 
 
 
• **Maxwell’s Corkscrew Rule**:
 
 
• Also known as the **Right-Hand Screw Rule**, it is used to find the direction of the **magnetic field** produced by a **current-carrying conductor**.
 
• If a right-handed **corkscrew** is rotated so that it moves forward in the direction of the **current**, then the direction of rotation of the handle indicates the direction of the **magnetic field lines**.
 
 
 
• **Right-Hand Thumb Rule**:
 
 
• This rule is used to determine the direction of **magnetic field lines** around a straight **current-carrying wire**.
 
• If the **thumb** of the right hand points in the direction of the **current**, the curled **fingers** show the direction of the **magnetic field**.
 
 
 
• **Fleming’s Right-Hand Rule**:
 
 
• This rule is used to find the direction of the **induced current** when a conductor moves inside a magnetic field (phenomenon of **Electromagnetic Induction**).
 
• It is primarily applied in **Electric Generators**. In this rule, the **thumb** represents motion, the **forefinger** represents the field, and the **middle finger** represents the **induced current**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Lorentz Force**: The force experienced by a charge moving in a magnetic field is given by **F = q(v × B)**. For a conductor of length **L**, the force is **F = BIL sinθ**.
 
• The force is **maximum** when the conductor is placed **perpendicular** (at **90 degrees**) to the magnetic field.
 
• The force is **zero** when the conductor is placed **parallel** or anti-parallel (at **0 or 180 degrees**) to the direction of the magnetic field.
 
• **John Ambrose Fleming**, a British physicist, devised these rules in the late **19th century** to provide an easy way for students to remember the orientation of vectors in **electromagnetism**.

questions.question: Which of the following is a traditional water harvesting method in Rajasthan, India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Johad**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Johad** is a traditional **rainwater harvesting** structure used in India, particularly in the state of **Rajasthan**. It is a **crescent-shaped** small earthen **check dam** built across a contour to capture and conserve rainwater runoff.
 
• The primary purpose of a **Johad** is to facilitate **groundwater recharge**. By holding rainwater, it allows the water to slowly percolate into the **aquifers**, thereby raising the **water table** in **arid** and **semi-arid** regions. ***Hence, the correct answer is Johad.***
 
• This traditional technique was revived significantly in the **Alwar district** of **Rajasthan** during the **1980s** and **1990s**. The revival led to the restoration of several dead rivers, such as the **Arvari River**.
 
• The **Tarun Bharat Sangh (TBS)**, an **NGO** led by **Rajendra Singh** (often called the **"Waterman of India"**), played a pivotal role in promoting **Johads**. Since **1985**, thousands of these structures have been built across **Rajasthan**, transforming the local ecology and **agriculture**.
 
• **Johads** are community-driven projects that require low maintenance and use locally available materials like **soil** and **stones**, making them a sustainable solution for **water scarcity**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hand pump:**
 
 
• A **hand pump** is a **manual device** used to extract water from a **well** or an **underground aquifer**. It is a **modern mechanical extraction** method rather than a **water harvesting** technique.
 
• While widely used in **rural India** for providing **drinking water**, it relies on existing **groundwater** levels rather than contributing to their replenishment.
 
 
 
• **Borewell:**
 
 
• A **borewell** is a deep, narrow hole drilled into the earth to reach deep-seated **groundwater**. It typically uses **electric or diesel pumps** for water extraction.
 
• Unlike **Johads**, **borewells** are a **modern intervention** that can lead to the **depletion of groundwater** if overused without proper **recharge mechanisms**.
 
 
 
• **Check dam:**
 
 
• A **check dam** is a small, sometimes temporary, dam constructed across a **swale**, **drainage ditch**, or **waterway** to counteract **erosion** and reduce water **velocity**.
 
• While a **Johad** is technically a type of earthen **check dam**, the term "**check dam**" is a general **civil engineering** term, whereas "**Johad**" refers specifically to the **traditional** and **cultural** practice unique to **Rajasthan**.
 
 
 
• **Other Traditional Methods in Rajasthan:**
 
 
• **Khadin:** A long earthen embankment built across the lower hill slopes to collect **runoff water** for **moisture-retention** in **agricultural** fields.
 
• **Tanka:** An **underground storage tank** used to collect **rainwater** from rooftops or prepared **catchment areas**, primarily used for **drinking purposes** in the **Thar Desert**.
 
• **Baori / Stepwell:** Magnificent **architectural structures** built to reach the **water table**, serving as **community reservoirs** for centuries.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Rajendra Singh:** Known as the **Waterman of India**, he won the **Ramon Magsaysay Award** in **2001** and the **Stockholm Water Prize** in **2015** for his work in **water conservation** and the revival of **Johads**.
 
• **Environmental Impact:** The use of **Johads** has been proven to increase **forest cover**, improve **crop yields**, and mitigate the effects of **drought** in the **Arid Zone**.
 
• **Geographical Context:** These structures are most effective in the **Aravalli Range** and the **Western Rajasthan** landscape, where the **soil type** allows for efficient **seepage** and **recharge**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following is a combination reaction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**CaO + H2O → Ca(OH)2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **combination reaction** (also known as a synthesis reaction) is a reaction where **two or more elements or compounds** combine to form a **single compound**. The general form is **A + B → AB**.
 
• In the reaction **CaO + H2O → Ca(OH)2**, **Calcium Oxide** (quicklime) reacts vigorously with **water** to produce **Calcium Hydroxide** (slaked lime). Since two reactants combine to form one single product, it is a classic example of a **combination reaction**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• The reaction **2KClO3 → 2KCl + 3O2** involves a single reactant breaking down into two or more simpler products. This is categorized as a **decomposition reaction**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The reaction **Fe + CuSO4 → FeSO4 + Cu** involves a more reactive element (**Iron**) displacing a less reactive element (**Copper**) from its salt solution. This is known as a **single displacement reaction**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The reaction **AgNO3 + NaCl → AgCl + NaNO3** involves an exchange of ions between two compounds to form two new compounds. This is a **double displacement reaction**, specifically a precipitation reaction as **AgCl** forms a white solid. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Combination Reactions:**
 
 
• These reactions are often **exothermic** in nature because bonds are formed, which releases energy.
 
• Examples include the **burning of coal** (C + O2 → CO2) and the **formation of water** from hydrogen and oxygen (2H2 + O2 → 2H2O).
 
• In the **CaO** reaction mentioned above, a large amount of **heat energy** is released, making the container hot.
 
 
 
• **Decomposition Reactions:**
 
 
• These are the opposite of combination reactions. They require energy in the form of **heat, light, or electricity** to break bonds.
 
• **Thermal decomposition** occurs when heat is used (e.g., heating Calcium Carbonate). **Electrolytic decomposition** occurs via electricity (e.g., electrolysis of water).
 
 
 
• **Displacement Reactions:**
 
 
• These depend on the **reactivity series** of metals. A metal placed higher in the series can displace a metal placed lower.
 
• For example, **Zinc** can displace copper from copper sulphate because Zinc is more reactive than Copper.
 
 
 
• **Double Displacement Reactions:**
 
 
• Usually occur in **aqueous solutions** where ions "switch partners."
 
• Commonly result in the formation of an insoluble solid called a **precipitate** or the formation of stable molecules like water in **neutralization reactions**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Calcium Oxide (CaO):** Commonly known as **quicklime** or burnt lime. It is widely used in the manufacture of **cement** and glass.
 
• **Calcium Hydroxide (Ca(OH)2):** Known as **slaked lime**. A dilute solution of slaked lime is called **lime water**.
 
• **White Washing:** The slaked lime produced in the combination reaction is used for **whitewashing walls**. It reacts slowly with **Carbon Dioxide** (CO2) in the air to form a thin, shiny layer of **Calcium Carbonate** (CaCO3) after **two to three days**.
 
• **Chemical Equations:** To satisfy the **Law of Conservation of Mass**, chemical equations must be **balanced**, meaning the number of atoms of each element must be equal on both the reactant and product sides.
